hints: Do not think only of the nucleus and cytoplasm. Ask yourself what is found inside the mitochondria (and chloroplasts in plants) of a typical eukaryotic cell.
Remember the endosymbiont idea: mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own tiny genomes and their own small ribosomes, similar to prokaryotes.
walkthrough:
**Start with what you know for sure**

Think of a typical animal or plant cell. In the cytoplasm and on rough ER you have large 80S ribosomes for protein synthesis. In the nucleus you have long linear DNA organised as chromosomes. So 2 and 3 are definitely present.

**Look inside the organelles**

A typical eukaryotic cell also contains mitochondria, and plant cells contain chloroplasts too. These organelles have their own DNA and their own ribosomes to make some of their own proteins.

**Recall the prokaryote-like features**

Because of their bacterial origin, mitochondria and chloroplasts contain small circular DNA loops (not linear chromosomes) and small 70S ribosomes (not 80S). So 1 and 4 are also present. That gives 1, 2, 3 and 4.

options.A: Correct. Eukaryotes have 80S in the cytoplasm plus 70S in mitochondria and chloroplasts, and linear DNA in the nucleus plus circular DNA in mitochondria and chloroplasts.
options.B: Misses out circular DNA. Mitochondria (and chloroplasts) contain small circular DNA loops, so 4 should be included.
options.C: Misses out the main features. It forgets the 80S ribosomes of the cytoplasm and the linear chromosomes of the nucleus.
options.D: Only the obvious features. It forgets the 70S ribosomes and circular DNA hidden inside mitochondria and chloroplasts.
